subject: Re: RFP - Throughput & Latency Validation: test plan and evidence
messages:
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@globex.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: enterprise-eng@globex.com
Date: 2026-07-12T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: Throughput / latency validation - initial questions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking our RFP. To evaluate Redwood for our production inference layer we need a concise description of how you measure and report latency/throughput. Specifically we need:

- Definitions for reported metrics (P50, P95, P99) and measurement windows
- How you measure per-request end-to-end latency (client -> Redwood -> model -> client)
- Typical QPS/throughput numbers for a 13B and 70B class model (warm and cold)
- Cold-start behavior and sample recovery times when scaling from zero replicas
- Concurrency and batching behavior (how batch size and concurrency interact)
- Failure and graceful degradation modes at saturation (what falls back and what fails fast)
- Test harness reproducibility and required artifacts (scripts, env spec, raw logs)

We would also like a short run from your lab that mimics a bursty traffic profile (sustained 400qps with 1.5k qps spikes) showing P50/P95/P99 and throughput, and the config used (hardware, model, quantization, batching, warmup procedure).

Please include attachments or links to the test spec and any CSV/aggregate output you can share. We will treat any detailed performance attachments as technical evaluation docs (not public).

Best,
Alice
Alice Turner
Senior Infrastructure PM, Globex Corporation

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@globex.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-13T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Throughput / latency validation - initial questions

Hi Alice — thanks, understood. Attached is our test specification and a proposed run plan (redwood_throughput_test_spec.pdf). High level answers inline below, and a proposed schedule for a reproducible lab run:

Summary answers (short):
- Metrics: we report end-to-end latency as observed at the API ingress in ms. All percentiles (P50/P95/P99) are computed on server-side latencies after deduping and removing explicit client timeouts. We include cpu/gpu utilization and per-token generation time in the CSV.
- End-to-end: measurement point is the API gateway request completion time. We include request/response timestamps and per-token timings from the runtime.
- Model classes: for a Redwood-verified 13B we expect baseline sustained throughput ~60–120 qps per GPU depending on sequence length; 70B ranges ~10–40 qps per GPU (these are warm steady-state numbers using fp16 / q4_0 quantized runtime on A100/H100-class hardware). Exacts are in the spec table.
- Cold start: VM/provisioning is not in scope for our hosted product: cold start refers to model loading and kv-cache warmup. Typical model load+initialization for 13B ≈ 8–20s; 70B ≈ 25–60s depending on kernel compilation and quantization. We capture first-request latencies separately.
- Concurrency & batching: runtime does automatic continuous batching where throughput improves with concurrency up to the model/hw cap. The spec lists concurrency sweep procedure (stepwise increase, hold periods, and histogram capture).
- Degradation: fallback paths include routing to a compatible lower-capacity model variant, and auto-throttle (429) when estimates exceed configured burst tolerance. We include details on deterministic graceful degradation in section 4.

Proposed reproducible run (we can run this in our lab or provide the harness so Globex runs it):
- Traffic profile: 60s warmup, 10m sustained 400 qps target with random Poisson bursts (peak 1500 qps for 15s every 2m).
- Metrics captured: per-request latency (ingress), per-token, GPU util, memory pressure, queue depth, batch sizes, error counts, and per-replica throughput.
- Artifacts: CSV of raw events, aggregated percentiles, flamegraphs of kernel times, and the run-config YAML.

I'll attach the test spec PDF and can run an initial lab job on Thursday morning PST if that works. If you prefer, we can share the harness and env matrix and you can run it inside a Globex-managed project.

Next steps:
- Confirm whether you want Redwood to run the lab job or prefer to execute in your environment.
- If Redwood runs: confirm a 4-hour window Thursday AM PST for scheduled runs and an access window for post-run log delivery.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_throughput_test_spec.pdf (application/pdf)]

Hi Alice — looping in commercial context. A couple quick items from our side to align expectations:

- SLA framing: for production we offer latency SLOs per model class and committed throughput under Redwood Dedicated. The lab run is purely technical validation and will not be an SLA guarantee; if Globex needs SLA-backed numbers we can scope a Dedicated capacity trial and include it in the commercial term sheet.
- Canaries: we recommend a two-stage approach — lab run (Rishi runs) followed by a short shared canary in your staging environment to validate network and tenant-isolation behavior.
- Audit artifacts: we can provide the raw CSVs and a short exec summary (1 page) tailored for procurement.

We'll attach the sample run CSV after Rishi completes the job. Ben — can you confirm availability to coordinate the canary window with Globex infra?
